title: Master of Cyber, Intelligence, and Information Law (I) (LtCol to Maj) NMOS (4402), SJA to CMC
raw_text:
10. MOS 4417, Master of Cyber, Intelligence, and Information Law (I) (LtCol
to Maj) NMOS (4402), SJA to CMC

    a. Summary. A Master of Cyber Law has specialized education or skills
in the laws, regulations, and policies surrounding cybersecurity, cyber
operations, space operations, intelligence, or information operations.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must either:

            (a) Hold a Master of Laws degree (LL.M.) in cyber, space, or
intelligence law, or a related course of study, from an American Bar
Association accredited program at a civilian institution approved by Judge
Advocate Division (JAD).

            (b) Successfully complete a CCLEB, CPIB, or TLS selected
fellowship related to cyber, space, intelligence, or information law
established with a civilian department or agency through coordination between
Judge Advocate Division, MMOA, and the external department or agency.

            (c) Successfully complete a specialty program in national
security law from the Graduate Course at The Judge Advocate General’s Legal
Center and School, U.S. Army, including completion of all degree requirements
for an LL.M., completion of all course offerings in cyber law, and completion
of an individual professional paper on a cyber, space, intelligence, or
information operations law topic.

            (d) Be otherwise qualified through extensive practical
experience, as determined by Judge Advocate Division.

        (2) Must be in the rank of major or lieutenant Colonel. Judge
advocates who meet the other prerequisites as a captain will not receive the
additional MOS until promoted to the rank of major.

        (3) Security requirement: Must have a current single scope
background investigation/T5 investigation and adjudicated for sensitive
compartmented information (SCI) security clearance eligibility. Applications
for SCI security clearance eligibility must be submitted prior to attendance
at an LL.M. program.

    c. Requirements. Judge Advocate Division (JAD), in conjunction with DC,
M&RA (MMOA), is responsible for assignment of this AMOS. JAD will publish
additional guidance for an experiential track as authorized in paragraph
b(1)(d), above.

       d.   Duties

            (1) May serve in any other MOS 4402 billet.

        (2) Serve in billets requiring an understanding of cybersecurity,
cyber operations, space operations, intelligence, or information operations
law issues. Officers may serve as staff judge advocates, deputy staff judge

advocates, or cyberspace intelligence/information law attorneys for Marine
Corps or Joint commands.

    e.      Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
None.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
